about: EVERYTHING THE HOUSE CAN WIN, 793-1066 (Design/content/CHAINS.md, the grand rewards; Design/research_scale_to_fleets.md 2 and 4.5). One entry for each: id (the flag's name where it is a flag: flags are set with the effect 'flag <id>' and read as flag.<id>), kind, name, what_it_is (true to the period), how_won (plain: in words; when: the offer's condition in the engine's grammar of Cond.cs, which the loader would accept; cost: in the grammar of an option's cost; where: port ids; by: the act, card, count or chain that gives it), what_it_gives (plain rules for a programmer), from and to (years), inherited (does an heir keep it), source. (?) marks what was not checked against a source tonight. Prices are starting guesses on the scale of CHAINS.md. The text and riddle_reward entries are made from texts_793.json and riddles_793.json by a script, so every text is here with where it is had. A draft in the game's own file, for the user to overwrite. Written 4 Oct 2026.

ship.rule: The house may have a ship of this class: the part after the prefix is a class id of ship_classes_793.json (the entry's ship_class). The entry says whether the flag is the right to build or buy one, or the hull itself. One keel is always the merchant's own; every other needs a skipper (a partner or kin) and orders in words. Eight keels at the most (research_scale_to_fleets.md 7.3).

charter.rule: A lord's freedom from toll at one port (the part after the prefix is a port id). The toll card's 'Show the charter' does 'toll none' there. It is lent by its lord, carries a yearly render, and lapses at a change of king until renewed. An heir must ask for it again: one audience and a gift.

plot.rule: A house plot or storehouse at a port: a stock of your own there, a winter berth, the ground a factor stands on. A raid on the port takes the stock.

factor.rule: A trusted man who keeps your goods at a port, buys and sells by standing orders and writes by every ship. A person, with a keep of 120 d a year. At a succession his feeling toward the house is halved like everyone's: below 'friendly' he asks new terms or leaves.

partner.rule: A sworn partner who sails a second boat. Any flag with this prefix is one partner: chains name their own (unlock_partner_<a person's name>). A partnership ends with a death: the stock is divided and the heir is offered the oath again if the partner is still at least friendly.

pilot.rule: The knowledge of one named bar, strait or river, in one word after the prefix. It goes with the chart: the heir keeps it.

upgrade.rule: A thing fitted to one ship (ids here until Data/story/ship_upgrades_793.json exists). It is lost with the ship in a wreck.

work.rule: A work in a town, paid for or granted: unlock_work_<port id>_<what>. It stands whatever becomes of the house, and the town remembers who paid.

title.rule: A standing among men. Sworn or granted to one man: the heir is offered it on easier terms (half the cost, no waiting) but must take it himself. The thegn's right alone passes with the house, while the house keeps a ship.

relic.rule: A holy thing the house keeps. See relic_uses for what honest and dishonest men do with one.

heirloom.rule: A thing the house keeps and an heir inherits. It is never in the hold and cannot be lost in a wreck unless the entry says it is carried.

kin.rule: A marriage, a fostering, a tie made at the font, a kinsman brought home. Any flag with this prefix is one tie: chains name their own.

tongue.rule: Not a flag: a learned tongue, held by the engine as tongue.<name> (0, 0.5 or 1) and set with 'tongue <name> = f'. The id here is tongue_<name>.

letters.rule: Not a flag: Latin letters and runes, held by the engine as learned.latin and learned.runes (0 to 1) and raised with 'learn latin +f' and 'learn runes +f'.

memorial.rule: Not a flag the chains set: what can be done for the dead, with the real formulas. When one is made, set flag memorial_<kind>_<port id>; the chronicle's line for the dead man names it.

text.rule: Not a flag: a text in the chest, read by conditions as text.<id> and given with 'give_text <id>'. The chest goes to the heir whole. One entry here for every text of texts_793.json, with where it is had.

riddle_reward.rule: Not a flag: what answering a riddle or a set of riddles pays (riddles_793.json 'rewards'), listed here so that everything the house can win is in one file. 'inherited' is per entry.

relic_uses.about: What honest and dishonest men do with a relic. Each line is a thing the player can do with any unlock_relic_ flag; 'does' is in the engine's verbs where it has them.

honest.gives: The flag unlock_relic_<name> is cleared and the church has it. Standing there rises as for three alms. Your name is said at mass on the saint's day and there is a grave for you near the altar. The priest writes your letters without a fee.
honest.source: burial near the saints and gifts for the soul: the ordinary practice of the age; Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 20, for a merchant woman's gifts to holy places

honest.do: Keep it in the chest and carry it aboard
honest.gives: Christian hands take heart from it: in a storm or a chase the crew's heart falls half as fast. Men of the old faith aboard are not moved either way.
honest.source: Ansgar fled Hamburg in 845 carrying the relics before anything else (chronicle_793.json 845-hamburg-burned)

honest.gives: An oath sworn on relics binds more than one sworn on a man's cloak or on a coin: in a lawsuit your oath and your oath-helpers' count one step better (doubtful to likely).
honest.source: Lex Frisionum distinguishes oaths 'in reliquiis sanctorum' from lesser oaths sworn on a garment or on money (?)

honest.gives: Once a winter. The priest approves; the wise woman shrugs.
honest.source: healing at a saint's relics: every saint's Life of the age, for instance Altfrid's Life of Liudger (the blind singer Bernlef)

honest.gives: An audience and a gift (60 d). A proven relic is worth three times as much to a church and cannot be called false afterwards. A false one is found out here, quietly.
honest.source: Council of Frankfurt 794 c. 42: no new saints to be honoured without authority

dishonest.gives: It becomes one unit of the good 'relics' in the hold and is sold like any cargo, best where a new church has no saint. The flag is cleared. If it came as a gift from a church, that church hears of it within the year: standing there falls as for a broken commission.
dishonest.source: Einhard, Translation of Marcellinus and Peter (827-828): the Roman deacon Deusdona dealt in martyrs' bones north of the Alps

dishonest.do: Divide it and sell the parts
dishonest.gives: Three units instead of one. None can ever be proven, and the first buyer who compares notes with the second knows your name.
dishonest.source: Einhard: part of his relics was stolen on the road by a rival's man and had to be begged back

dishonest.gives: A pig's knuckle in a scrap of silk sells once. Each later call at that port there is a 'doubtful' chance it has been found out: then 'deed taken_for_judgement'.
dishonest.source: Admonitio generalis 789 c. 42 (false names of martyrs) and c. 79 (wandering cheats who deceive people)

dishonest.gives: The lawsuit is won today. If the truth comes out (a 'doubtful' chance each year for three years), the law takes the hand that swore: the house is shunned in that realm.
dishonest.source: Capitulary of Herstal 779 c. 10: a perjurer loses his hand (?)

dishonest.do: Take one from a church in a raid year
dishonest.gives: When a church is burned or left empty after a raid, its relics lie where the monks hid them. Taking them is sacrilege to every Christian who hears of it; returning them to the monks instead is worth more than any alms.
dishonest.source: reputation_793.json dug_church_ground; the monks of Lindisfarne carried Cuthbert's body away in 875

unlocks.name: The house's own boat
unlocks.what_it_is: A small clinker boat with six oars and one square sail: 7.7 m, four men, under a ton of cargo. The boat she is modelled on was built about 1130 and found at Gislinge in Denmark; she stands in for the working boats of 793, which are known only from rivets and fragments.

how_won.plain: The house starts with her. After a wreck a new one is built over a winter by any wright of the delta, or bought used at a Danish landing.

unlocks.what_it_gives: Ship class gislinge. The first needs no flag. After a loss the flag is set when the new hull is paid for; ordered before Candlemas she is ready at Easter.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json gislinge (Viking Ship Museum, Roskilde: the Gislinge boat); price from CHAINS.md, a small boat about 600 d (?)

unlocks.name: A sea-going trader of the Frisian kind
unlocks.what_it_is: The ship in which Frisians, Franks and English crossed to Lundenwic, Eoforwic and Ripa: about 14 m, five men, six tons, a sail and a few oars. The ship struck on the Dorestad pennies of Louis the Pious is of this kind (?).

how_won.plain: Ordered from a wright over a winter. He builds only for a man the port knows, and the timber is paid in advance. Also the finale of a chain.
how_won.when: moored and standing >= known and silver >= 2400

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may build or buy ship class north_sea_merchant_ship. The old boat is kept as a second keel (she needs a skipper: a partner or kin) or sold for a third of her price.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json north_sea_merchant_ship; the Dorestad ship pennies of Louis the Pious, c. 814-840 (?); price from CHAINS.md, a sea-going trader several thousand d (?)

unlocks.name: A minster's coaster
unlocks.what_it_is: English minsters kept ships of their own, and the kings of Kent and Mercia let them off the toll: three ships of Minster-in-Thanet at Sarre and Fordwic (763 or 764), one ship of the bishop of Rochester at London (733). An abbess or bishop puts a trusted merchant in charge of such a ship.

how_won.plain: Keep three commissions for the same minster and be well regarded there. The abbess or bishop then asks you to take the house's ship for a season.
how_won.when: moored and standing >= well_regarded and (port.kind = monastery or port.id = sarre or port.id = fordwic)

unlocks.what_it_gives: Ship class coaster_minster_ship, lent, not owned: she is the minster's. While you sail her the minster's charter is yours at its port (unlock_charter_sarre, unlock_charter_fordwic or unlock_charter_lundenwic). Two thirds of the freight on the minster's own goods is the minster's. She goes back if your standing there falls below known, or if she is used to carry captives or arms.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json coaster_minster_ship; Sawyer S 29 (Eadberht II of Kent to Abbess Sigeburga, 763 or 764, with leave to replace a ship lost or broken); S 88 (Æthelbald of Mercia to the bishop of Rochester, 733): esawyer.lib.cam.ac.uk, read 4 Oct 2026

unlocks.name: A Rhine barge
unlocks.what_it_is: A flat-bottomed plank barge of about 16 m that carries seven tons of wine, querns and pots down the Rhine and is towed back up by men or oxen on the bank.

how_won.plain: Bought from a river wright at a Rhine town, or taken in payment of a debt.
how_won.when: moored and silver >= 900 and (port.id = colonia or port.id = mogontia or port.id = diusburg or port.id = dorestad)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class river_barge: rivers only, never the sea. She needs three men and a towing crew upstream (act:hire_porters). She is a second keel: give her to a skipper for the river haul while you take the sea.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json river_barge (the Krefeld-Gellep barges); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A river freighter on a log keel
unlocks.what_it_is: A hollowed and widened oak log with planks added: ten metres, three men, under two tons. The cheapest thing that will carry a cargo between Traiectum, Dorestad and Daventre.

how_won.plain: Bought at any landing on the Rhine branches.
how_won.when: moored and silver >= 250 and (port.id = traiectum or port.id = daventre or port.id = dorestad or port.id = noviomagus)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class logboat_expanded: rivers only. A cheap second keel for a kinsman to learn on.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json logboat_expanded (forerunner of the Utrecht type); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A Northman's ship of twelve oars
unlocks.what_it_is: The all-purpose ship of the Danes and Northmen, 12 to 18 m: she trades, carries envoys and carries a warband, and she both sails and rows well. Twelve men is her least crew.

how_won.plain: A Dane sells a ship only to a man he has eaten with: speak his tongue at least in part, be known at his port, and pay in silver by weight. A Vestfold chief gives one for the three sea riddles (riddle reward rw_ship_vestfold).
how_won.when: moored and tongue.old_norse >= 0.5 and standing >= known and silver >= 3000

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class norse_allround_ship. Twelve men to feed and pay: she earns only on the long northern runs. In Frankish and English waters before 878 a ship of this build is taken for a raider at first sight: the king's men close on her more often.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json norse_allround_ship; riddles_793.json rw_ship_vestfold; price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A four-oared boat of the north
unlocks.what_it_is: The small clinker boat of every Scandinavian shore, close kin to the house's own. The Gokstad ship of about 900 was buried with three of them.

how_won.plain: Bought at any Norse landing, or given as a partner's stake when goods are laid together.
how_won.when: moored and silver >= 250 and (port.realm = danes or port.realm = norse_vestfold or port.realm = norse_west or port.realm = svear or port.realm = gutes)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class norse_small_boat: a second keel for a partner on a short coasting run.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json norse_small_boat (the Gokstad small boats, c. 900: LATER stand-in); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A Wendish coasting boat
unlocks.what_it_is: The boat of the southern Baltic shore, ten metres, her planks held with wooden pegs where a Northman would use iron rivets.

how_won.plain: Bought at a Wendish, Prussian or Curonian market from a man whose tongue you have in part, or through a factor there.
how_won.when: moored and silver >= 500 and (port.id = reric or port.id = truso or port.id = grobin)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class baltic_coastal_boat. Light enough to drag over a sandbar, and a known shape on that coast: the Wends' own toll-takers ask fewer questions of her.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json baltic_coastal_boat (treenailed Slav boats; riveted boats at Truso and Grobina); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A hide boat of the Irish
unlocks.what_it_is: Ox hides tanned in oak bark, sewn over a frame of ash and greased with wool fat. In 891 three Irishmen came to King Alfred in a boat of two and a half hides, without oars, after seven days at sea.

how_won.plain: The monks of Hi or a boat-builder at Duiblinn make one for a man who has served the house: carried a letter or a brother, or kept a commission.
how_won.when: moored and standing >= known and (port.id = hi or port.id = duiblinn)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class currach. She carries little and lands on any beach; four men can carry her over a neck of land. She must be greased every month or she rots.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json currach; Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 891 (the three Irishmen); Adomnan, Life of Columba, for the monks' hide boats

unlocks.name: A bishop's or an abbey's river ship
unlocks.what_it_is: A lord's own ship for his wine, his salt and his people: 14 m and eight men. Great abbeys kept ships and men bound to sail them; the men of Prüm owed carrying service on the Rhine and the Moselle (the abbey's survey of 893).

how_won.plain: A bishop or abbot whose commissions you have kept three times asks you to master his ship for a season.
how_won.when: moored and standing >= well_regarded and port.realm = franks and (port.kind = town or port.kind = monastery)

unlocks.what_it_gives: Ship class river_estate_ship, lent: she is the lord's. His goods go toll-free in her wherever his charter runs. You may load your own goods beside his, which is the profit. She goes back when he dies or when you fail one of his errands.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json river_estate_ship; the Prüm survey of 893 for carrying services (?)

unlocks.name: A half-decked sea trader (from about 1000)
unlocks.what_it_is: The deep cargo ship of the late period: decked fore and aft, an open hold between, a small crew and a big belly. Skuldelev 1, built about 1030 in western Norway, was 16 m and carried some 24 tons with six to eight men; the Klåstad ship of the 990s carried 13.

how_won.plain: Built to order over a winter at a Norse or Danish yard for a house with a plot there, or bought from an Icelander abroad.
how_won.when: moored and year >= 1000 and silver >= 6000 and tongue.old_norse >= 0.5

unlocks.what_it_gives: The right to a ship of this kind. THE CLASS IS NOT IN ship_classes_793.json YET (it is in its later_types_not_in_table): until a row is added, the flag does nothing.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json later_types_not_in_table; research_scale_to_fleets.md section 2 (24 tons, six to eight men); the Skuldelev ships, Viking Ship Museum, Roskilde

unlocks.name: The great trader of Hedeby (from about 1025)
unlocks.what_it_is: The largest cargo ship known from the age: the wreck called Hedeby 3, built about 1025, some 22 m long and able to carry about 60 tons.

how_won.plain: Only a house with a plot at Sliesthorp, a partner there and the king's man's good will can order one.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = sliesthorp and year >= 1025 and flag.unlock_plot_sliesthorp and standing >= trusted and silver >= 12000

unlocks.what_it_gives: The right to a ship of this kind. THE CLASS IS NOT IN ship_classes_793.json YET: until a row is added, the flag does nothing.
unlocks.source: research_scale_to_fleets.md section 2 (the Hedeby ship of about 1025 that carried 60 tons); Wikinger Museum Haithabu (?)

unlocks.name: A logboat
unlocks.what_it_is: One hollowed oak trunk, about five metres, paddled or poled by one or two men. The oldest boat there is and still the commonest on every river and creek. One was built into a landing at Welham Bridge in Yorkshire between about 530 and 690, and one from Callow in Ireland is of the ninth century.

how_won.plain: Bought from any river man for a few pennies, or cut over a fortnight by your own men from a trunk you have paid for.
how_won.when: moored and silver >= 20 and (port.id = dorestad or port.id = traiectum or port.id = daventre or port.id = noviomagus or port.id = medemelacha or port.id = eoforwic or port.id = truso or port.id = aldeigjuborg)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class logboat: rivers and sheltered creeks only, a third of a ton. No skipper is needed: a boy can take her. Use: an errand boat at a plot (word between the house and the quay a day sooner), and the boat a ruined man starts again with if the count has taken the other.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json logboat (Welham Bridge, Callow; McGrail 1978); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A skiff for the quay
unlocks.what_it_is: A short flat plank boat with one pair of oars or a pole, half a ton. The Salic law of the Franks, about 510, already sets fines for taking another man's boat; the London toll of about 1000 asks a halfpenny of a small boat at Billingsgate and a penny of a larger one with a sail.

how_won.plain: Bought at any Frankish, Frisian or English river port.
how_won.when: moored and silver >= 40 and (port.id = dorestad or port.id = traiectum or port.id = colonia or port.id = mogontia or port.id = parisius or port.id = rotomagus or port.id = lundenwic or port.id = eoforwic or port.id = quentovic)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class skiff_punt. Kept at a plot or a jetty she works as a lighter: a ship of the house that cannot come alongside is loaded and unloaded there without hired porters (act:hire_porters costs nothing at that port). She pays the small boat's toll, not the keel's.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json skiff_punt (Pactus legis Salicae title 21; IV Aethelred 2, Billingsgate, about 1000); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A small working boat of the coast
unlocks.what_it_is: A clinker boat of about six metres with four oars and sometimes a small sail, for nets, weirs and ferrying: the boat of the fishermen and the creek. Clench nails from such boats lie in graves at Dover, Caister and Barton on the Humber, and the great fish weirs of the Blackwater were worked from them.

how_won.plain: Bought used from a fisherman at any Frisian, Frankish or English landing, or built over six weeks by a wright.
how_won.when: moored and silver >= 150 and (port.id = dorestad or port.id = witla or port.id = walichrum or port.id = medemelacha or port.id = wijnaldum or port.id = doccinga or port.id = quentovic or port.id = sarre or port.id = fordwic or port.id = dofras or port.id = gipeswic or port.id = hamwic or port.id = dommoc)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class west_small_boat: coast and river, half a ton, two men. The cheapest hull that can go outside the dunes in fair weather: a first boat again after a wreck when 600 d is not to be had, or a boat for a son of fourteen to carry fish and salt between the terp landings.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json west_small_boat (Dover-Buckland, Caister-on-Sea, Castledyke; Blackwater weirs); price set at a quarter of the Gislinge boat's, a guess (?)

unlocks.name: The ferry at a crossing
unlocks.what_it_is: A wide flat barge that takes a cart and its oxen, two or three horses or twenty people over a river, poled or rowed. The ferry is a lord's right: Charlemagne's capitulary of Thionville in 805 allows a toll only where a bridge or a ferry is truly provided for the traveller.

how_won.plain: The count or the bishop farms the crossing to a man he trusts for a yearly render. Be trusted at the port, hold a plot there and pay the entry.
how_won.when: moored and standing >= trusted and silver >= 300 and (port.id = traiectum or port.id = daventre or port.id = noviomagus or port.id = colonia or port.id = mogontia or port.id = diusburg)

unlocks.what_it_gives: Ship class ferry_barge, which never leaves its crossing, and with it the right to the ferry toll there: about 60 d a year paid in at the winter reckoning, less a render of 20 d to the lord, and a ferryman's keep of 30 d. All who cross talk: rumours at that port are a week fresher. The right is the lord's and is asked for again by an heir (one audience and a gift); the barge itself stays the house's.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json ferry_barge; Capitulary of Thionville 805 c. 13 (toll only where a bridge or ferry is provided) (?); the sums are guesses (?)

unlocks.name: A timber raft
unlocks.what_it_is: Logs lashed into a platform and steered down a river with poles and sweeps. The raft is the cargo: it is broken up and sold at the end. Bede tells of monks bringing timber down the Tyne on rafts when a west wind carried them out to sea, and Cuthbert, a boy on the bank, prayed them back.

how_won.plain: Buy standing timber upriver in winter, hire four raftmen and bring it down on the spring water.
how_won.when: moored and silver >= 200 and month >= 3 and month <= 5 and (port.id = mogontia or port.id = colonia or port.id = diusburg or port.id = daventre)

unlocks.what_it_gives: One voyage of ship class raft, downstream only, about 30 km a day: no flag is needed after the first, which only teaches the trade. At the river mouth the raft is sold as ten tons of oak to a shipwright (about twice its cost at Dorestad or Traiectum, more in a year after a fire or a raid) or kept: a ship of the house built that winter from your own timber costs a quarter less.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json raft (Bede, Prose Life of Cuthbert ch. 3); rafting on the Rhine in these years is likely but not attested (?); the sums are guesses (?)

unlocks.name: A seven-bencher of the western sea
unlocks.what_it_is: The plank-built rowing ship of the Irish Sea kindreds, about eleven metres, seven benches and a sail. The Senchus fer nAlban, a reckoning of Dal Riata, asks two seven-benchers from every twenty houses for the sea muster. She carries men, not cargo: two tons at the most.

how_won.plain: A lord of the kindred or the abbot of Hi gives the right to have one built to a stranger who is trusted there and speaks the tongue.
how_won.when: moored and standing >= trusted and tongue.irish >= 0.5 and silver >= 900 and (port.id = hi or port.id = duiblinn)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class gaelic_wooden_ship. Fourteen oars make her nearly free of the wind among the islands, and no small raider will try her; but sixteen men eat what two tons of cargo earn. Worth having only for carrying people who pay: monks, envoys, relics, a bride.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json gaelic_wooden_ship (Senchus fer nAlban; Adomnan, Life of Columba: navis longa); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A place at the steering oar of a levy ship
unlocks.what_it_is: A long rowing ship of the king's levy, twenty to sixty men. It is never a merchant's own. Frisians came by ship up the Havel for Charlemagne in 789; from 800 he set guards on the coast and in 811 fleets at Boulogne and Ghent; in 896 Alfred built long ships of sixty oars, and Wulfheard, Aebbe and Aethelhere, Frisians, died in them; in 1008 Aethelred ordered a ship from every 310 hides.

how_won.plain: It is a duty, not a prize. A shipowner who is trusted where the levy is called is told to bring his men and steer, or to pay for a man who will.
how_won.when: moored and standing >= trusted and year >= 800 and (port.id = dorestad or port.id = walichrum or port.id = ganda or port.id = quentovic or port.id = lundenwic or port.id = hamwic or port.id = dofras)

unlocks.what_it_gives: No ship is owned: the flag marks that the merchant has steered the king's ship (set with flag levy_served by the winter card). For that summer his own boat sails under his steersman on shares, or lies ashore. It gives the lord's good will (npc feeling up, a toll eased for a year), the deed for serving, and the men who rowed beside him as hands to hire. It counts toward unlock_title_kings_protection and unlock_title_thegn. A man who neither serves nor pays is fined the heerban: sixty shillings by the capitularies (720 d), which ruins a small house.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json warship_west; Royal Frankish Annals 789, 800, 811; Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 896 (897 in some texts) and 1008; the heerban of 60 solidi, Capitulary of Boulogne 811 (?)

unlocks.name: A warship of the Northmen
unlocks.what_it_is: The raiders' ship: eighteen to twenty-seven metres, thirty oars and more, thirty-five men, and room for two tons. The ship buried at Storhaug on Karmoy was built about 770 with a keel of some twenty-two metres; the Oseberg ship was built in 820. A king or a jarl has one built and mans it with sworn men.

how_won.plain: A merchant does not win one. A Norse lord whose guest-right you hold may sell an old one, or leave you one he has taken, and then only to a man who speaks his tongue.
how_won.when: moored and flag.unlock_title_danish_guest_right and tongue.old_norse >= 1 and silver >= 4000 and (port.id = sliesthorp or port.id = skiringssal or port.id = ogvaldsnes or port.id = hleidr)

unlocks.what_it_gives: The house may own ship class norse_longship, and should think twice. She needs thirty men at the oars who are fed whether she earns or not, and carries two tons. Every Christian port treats her as a raider on sight: the harbour is shut, the watch is called, and standing in that region falls unless a charter or a lord's letter is shown first. In heathen waters small raiders leave her alone. Fit for carrying a lord and his men for pay, for convoying the house's own traders, and for nothing honest besides.
unlocks.source: ship_classes_793.json norse_longship (Storhaug, built about 770: Bill and Daly 2012; Oseberg, built 820); that lords sold or gave old ships to merchants is a guess from later sagas (?); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: Saint-Germain's freedom at Dorestad
unlocks.what_it_is: In 779 Charlemagne freed the abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés from the king's toll at Quentovic, Rouen, Amiens, Maastricht and Dorestad. The freedom belongs to the abbey. A merchant has it only while he carries the abbey's goods and its letter.

how_won.plain: Carry for the abbey three times between the Seine and the Rhine mouth without loss and be known at Parisius; the cellarer then gives you the abbey's letter. A riddle gives the same freedom for some years (riddle reward rw_toll_dorestad).
how_won.when: moored and port.id = parisius and standing >= known

unlocks.what_it_gives: While the flag is set, the toll man's option 'Show the charter' is open at this port and does 'toll none' (harbour.tollman.frankish checks text.charter_toll_dorestad today: let it also read flag.unlock_charter_<port id>). Render: each year before the fair of Saint-Denis (9 October) bring the abbey six units of frisian_cloth and four of wax, sold to it at the market price with no premium. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: Charter of Charlemagne for Saint-Germain-des-Prés, 779 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentovic, read 4 Oct 2026; MGH DD Karol. I, number not checked (?)); economy_and_trade.md 1.4; riddles_793.json rw_toll_dorestad

unlocks.name: Saint-Germain's freedom at Quentovic
unlocks.what_it_is: The same grant of 779 names Quentovic first. The king's toll there was a tenth, taken by his procurator: from about 787 Gervold, abbot of Saint-Wandrille, who knew King Offa.

how_won.plain: As at Dorestad: the abbey's letter, won at Parisius or Rotomagus by carrying for it.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = parisius or port.id = rotomagus) and standing >= known

unlocks.what_it_gives: While the flag is set, the toll man's option 'Show the charter' is open at this port and does 'toll none' (harbour.tollman.frankish checks text.charter_toll_dorestad today: let it also read flag.unlock_charter_<port id>). Render: two casks of frankish_wine carried to the abbey's cell free of freight each year. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: Charter of 779 as above; Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12 for Gervold (npc_roles_793.json harbour_master); the Edict of Pîtres, 864, is the last mention of Quentovic

unlocks.name: Saint-Germain's freedom at Rotomagus
unlocks.what_it_is: Rouen is the third toll named in the grant of 779: the abbey's wine came down the Seine through it.

how_won.plain: The abbey's letter, as at Dorestad and Quentovic.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = parisius and standing >= known

unlocks.what_it_gives: While the flag is set, the toll man's option 'Show the charter' is open at this port and does 'toll none' (harbour.tollman.frankish checks text.charter_toll_dorestad today: let it also read flag.unlock_charter_<port id>). No render beyond the abbey's own freight. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it. After 911 the tolls of Rouen are the Norman count's and the old letter is worth nothing.
unlocks.source: Charter of 779 as above; the grant of Rouen to Rollo, 911

unlocks.name: The freedom of the fair of Saint-Denis
unlocks.what_it_is: The fair that opens on Saint Denis's day, 9 October. King Pippin in 753 confirmed that all its tolls are the abbey's and not the count of Paris's; Frisians and Saxons are named among those who came.

how_won.plain: Bring the abbey what it lacks at the fair three years running (wax, honey, madder, northern cloth) and the abbot's steward enters your name among the abbey's own merchants.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = parisius and standing >= well_regarded

unlocks.what_it_gives: During the fair (fairs_793.json: 28 days from 9 October) you pay no toll at Parisius: 'toll none'. A riddle gives another right there, the sole right to sell pepper at the fair (riddle reward rw_right_pepper). The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: Diploma of Pippin for Saint-Denis, 753 (fairs_793.json: the fair of Saint-Denis, confirmed by Pippin 753 and Charles 775); riddles_793.json rw_right_pepper

unlocks.name: A bishop's ship at Lundenwic
unlocks.what_it_is: King Æthelbald of Mercia let the bishop of Rochester off the toll on one ship at London in 733, and King Berhtwulf confirmed it between 844 and 851. The bishop of Worcester and the abbess of Minster-in-Thanet held the like (?). The freedom goes with the ship, whoever masters her.

how_won.plain: Master a minster's or a bishop's ship (unlock_ship_coaster_minster_ship), or win the reeve's leave by a chain. A riddle gives the same for some years (riddle reward rw_toll_lundenwic).
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = lundenwic or port.id = sarre or port.id = fordwic) and standing >= well_regarded

unlocks.what_it_gives: At Lundenwic the reeve's toll is not taken on this one ship: 'toll none'. One ship only: a second keel of the house pays. It holds only while the ship carries the church's goods along with yours. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: Sawyer S 88 (733, confirmed by Berhtwulf 844 x 851): esawyer.lib.cam.ac.uk, read 4 Oct 2026; S 98 (Worcester, two ships) and S 86, S 87 (Minster-in-Thanet) from memory (?); riddles_793.json rw_toll_lundenwic. After 871 the Danes winter in London; the walled city of 886 has other rules

unlocks.name: The abbess's ships at Sarre
unlocks.what_it_is: In 763 or 764 King Eadberht of Kent let Abbess Sigeburga of Minster-in-Thanet off the toll on her ships at Sarre and Fordwic, three in all, with leave to put another in the place of one lost or broken.

how_won.plain: Master one of the abbess's ships, or be named by her as the man who replaces a ship she has lost.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = sarre or port.id = fordwic) and standing >= well_regarded

unlocks.what_it_gives: At Sarre no toll on this ship: 'toll none'. The clause on a lost ship is yours too: if she is wrecked, the next ship you bring has the freedom at once. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: Sawyer S 29: esawyer.lib.cam.ac.uk, read 4 Oct 2026. The end year is a guess from the raids on Thanet and Sheppey (835, 851) (?)

unlocks.name: The abbess's ship at Fordwic
unlocks.what_it_is: The same grant of 763 or 764: one of the three ships is free at Fordwic, the landing for Canterbury on the Stour.

how_won.plain: As at Sarre. A riddle gives the same for some years (riddle reward rw_toll_fordwic).
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = sarre or port.id = fordwic) and standing >= well_regarded

unlocks.what_it_gives: At Fordwic no toll on this ship: 'toll none'. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: Sawyer S 29, as above; riddles_793.json rw_toll_fordwic

unlocks.name: Saint Martin's man at Traiectum
unlocks.what_it_is: The church of Saint Martin at Utrecht held by the kings' gift a tenth of the king's dues in its lands, and from 777 the upper church at Dorestad with the bank dues there. A man who settles on the church's ground and carries for the bishop is under its immunity.

how_won.plain: Take a plot on the bishop's ground or keep three of his commissions; then ask it of him at an audience, with a gift.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = traiectum and standing >= well_regarded

unlocks.what_it_gives: While the flag is set, the toll man's option 'Show the charter' is open at this port and does 'toll none' (harbour.tollman.frankish checks text.charter_toll_dorestad today: let it also read flag.unlock_charter_<port id>). Render: a tenth of what you land at Traiectum is offered first to the bishop's cellarer at the market price. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it. It does not run at Dorestad, where the king's tenth is still taken.
unlocks.source: Charter of Charlemagne for the church of Utrecht, 8 June 777 (nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorestad, read 4 Oct 2026); the tenth of the royal dues from Pippin's and Charles's confirmations, from memory (?). Utrecht was sacked in 857 and the bishops lived at Deventer until about 920: it runs again after that (?)

unlocks.name: The bishop of Strasbourg's freedom on the Rhine
unlocks.what_it_is: Charlemagne gave the men of the church of Strasbourg freedom from toll through the whole realm, except at Quentovic, at Dorestad and at the Alpine passes, and Louis the Pious confirmed it in 831. Their boats came down the Rhine to the Frisian sea with wine and went home with what Frisia sold.

how_won.plain: Carry the bishop's wine down to the delta three times and be well regarded at Mogontia.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = mogontia or port.id = colonia) and standing >= well_regarded

unlocks.what_it_gives: No toll at Mogontia, Colonia and Diusburg ('toll none': it also sets unlock_charter_colonia and unlock_charter_diusburg). It says in so many words that it does not run at Dorestad or Quentovic: there the tenth is paid. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: Privilege of Charlemagne for the church of Strasbourg (c. 775), confirmed by Louis the Pious in 831: from memory, numbers not checked (?)

unlocks.name: The bishop of Strasbourg's freedom at Colonia
unlocks.what_it_is: The same freedom as at Mogontia: the men of the church of Strasbourg pay no toll on the Rhine below their city, down to where the king's own tenth begins at Dorestad.

how_won.plain: It comes with unlock_charter_mogontia and is lost with it.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = mogontia or port.id = colonia) and standing >= well_regarded

unlocks.what_it_gives: While the flag is set, the toll man's option 'Show the charter' is open at this port and does 'toll none' (harbour.tollman.frankish checks text.charter_toll_dorestad today: let it also read flag.unlock_charter_<port id>). Set and cleared together with unlock_charter_mogontia. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: as unlock_charter_mogontia: from memory, not checked (?)

unlocks.name: The bishop of Strasbourg's freedom at Diusburg
unlocks.what_it_is: The same freedom as at Mogontia: the men of the church of Strasbourg pay no toll on the Rhine below their city, down to where the king's own tenth begins at Dorestad.

how_won.plain: It comes with unlock_charter_mogontia and is lost with it.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = mogontia or port.id = colonia) and standing >= well_regarded

unlocks.what_it_gives: While the flag is set, the toll man's option 'Show the charter' is open at this port and does 'toll none' (harbour.tollman.frankish checks text.charter_toll_dorestad today: let it also read flag.unlock_charter_<port id>). Set and cleared together with unlock_charter_mogontia. The freedom is the lord's, not yours: it lapses if you carry captives or arms under it, if your standing with the lord's house falls below known, and when the king who gave or confirmed it dies (a chronicle entry of kind 'accession' in that realm), until an audience and a gift renew it.
unlocks.source: as unlock_charter_mogontia: from memory, not checked (?)

unlocks.name: A plot on the bank at Dorestad
unlocks.what_it_is: Dorestad's waterfront was cut into long narrow plots, each with its house at the top and its own timber causeway running down to the river, lengthened every few years as the Rhine moved away east.

how_won.plain: Bought from the count's man, or from a widow who is leaving, by a house the port knows.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and standing >= known and silver >= 400

unlocks.what_it_gives: A stock of your own at this port (the House tab, Stores): goods left there are not aboard; buy in the cheap season, sell in the dear. A free winter berth and a roof for the crew. A factor needs it. The plot is an instance of works_793.json plot: 12 d a year to the lord of the port at Martinmas, and the house works (storehouse, well, jetty, sheds) are built on it; the price is this port's own. Each few years the causeway must be lengthened (unlock_work_dorestad_jetty) or big ships cannot lie at it. The danger grows with it: a chronicle raid or burning at this port takes the stock unless it was moved or buried. Rumour comes first.
unlocks.source: Excavations at Wijk bij Duurstede, Hoogstraat (van Es and Verwers, 1967-1977) (?); chronicle_793.json 834-dorestad-sacked and after; price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A plot at Daventre
unlocks.what_it_is: When Dorestad's river silted and the raids came every year, its trade went up the IJssel to Deventer and up the Waal to Tiel. The Northmen burned the 'port' of Deventer in 882, so there was a port to burn.

how_won.plain: Bought from the bishop's steward. A house that had a plot at Dorestad is offered one first.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = daventre and year >= 850 and silver >= 300

unlocks.what_it_gives: A stock of your own at this port (the House tab, Stores): goods left there are not aboard; buy in the cheap season, sell in the dear. A free winter berth and a roof for the crew. A factor needs it. The plot is an instance of works_793.json plot: 12 d a year to the lord of the port at Martinmas, and the house works (storehouse, well, jetty, sheds) are built on it; the price is this port's own. A house that holds unlock_plot_dorestad when Dorestad ends (863) may move its stock here at no cost. The danger grows with it: a chronicle raid or burning at this port takes the stock unless it was moved or buried. Rumour comes first.
unlocks.source: Annales Fuldenses 882 (Deventer burned) (?); chronicle_793.json 863-dorestad-last; price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A market plot at Ripa
unlocks.what_it_is: Ribe's market place was laid out soon after 700 as a row of narrow plots divided by ditches along the river, where comb-makers, bead-makers and traders set up for the season.

how_won.plain: Given by the king's man at Ripa for a yearly gift, to a trader who has come three summers.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = ripa and standing >= known and silver >= 200

unlocks.what_it_gives: A stock of your own at this port (the House tab, Stores): goods left there are not aboard; buy in the cheap season, sell in the dear. A free winter berth and a roof for the crew. A factor needs it. The plot is an instance of works_793.json plot: 12 d a year to the lord of the port at Martinmas, and the house works (storehouse, well, jetty, sheds) are built on it; the price is this port's own. No coin toll here: the king's man is paid in gifts, and a plot-holder's gift is fixed (20 d of silver by weight each summer).
unlocks.source: Excavations at Ribe (Feveile and Jensen): plots laid out c. 705-710 (?); fairs_793.json, the summer market at Ripa; price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A plot at Sliesthorp
unlocks.what_it_is: In 808 King Godfred destroyed the Wendish market of Reric and moved its merchants to his own port of Sliesthorp, the place later called Hedeby: fenced plots along a brook, and jetties built out into the bay.

how_won.plain: From 808 the king's man gives plots to merchants who will stay. A house with a stock at Reric is moved here whether it likes it or not.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = sliesthorp and year >= 808 and standing >= known and silver >= 300

unlocks.what_it_gives: A stock of your own at this port (the House tab, Stores): goods left there are not aboard; buy in the cheap season, sell in the dear. A free winter berth and a roof for the crew. A factor needs it. The plot is an instance of works_793.json plot: 12 d a year to the lord of the port at Martinmas, and the house works (storehouse, well, jetty, sheds) are built on it; the price is this port's own. From about 825 the king's coin is struck here. From about 850 there is a church, and Christian merchants of Dorestad and Hamburg come without fear. The danger grows with it: a chronicle raid or burning at this port takes the stock unless it was moved or buried. Rumour comes first.
unlocks.source: Annales regni Francorum 808 (chronicle_793.json 808-summer-reric-destroyed); Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 24 (chronicle_793.json 850-hedeby-church); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A plot in the Black Earth at Birka
unlocks.what_it_is: Birka's town on its island in the lake of the Svear: plots running down to stone jetties, in soil black with a town's leavings. The king's prefect answers for the place.

how_won.plain: Leave of the prefect, a gift to him, and a winter spent there or a factor left there.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = birka and tongue.old_norse >= 0.5 and standing >= known and silver >= 300

unlocks.what_it_gives: A stock of your own at this port (the House tab, Stores): goods left there are not aboard; buy in the cheap season, sell in the dear. A free winter berth and a roof for the crew. A factor needs it. The plot is an instance of works_793.json plot: 12 d a year to the lord of the port at Martinmas, and the house works (storehouse, well, jetty, sheds) are built on it; the price is this port's own. Silver goes by weight here. The lake is shut by ice from about Martinmas to April: what is not sent out by Michaelmas waits a winter.
unlocks.source: Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 11 and 19 (the prefect Herigar); chronicle_793.json 975-birka-sigtuna; price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A house on the Strand, later a plot at the hythe
unlocks.what_it_is: Until the Danes wintered there in 871, London's market was the open strand west of the old walls. In 886 King Alfred restored the walled city, and plots at Æthelred's hythe were granted in 889 and 898 or 899 to the bishop of Worcester and the archbishop of Canterbury, with the right to moor ships and hold a market.

how_won.plain: Before 871: bought from the reeve by a house well regarded at Lundenwic. From 889: leased from a bishop who holds a plot at the hythe.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = lundenwic and standing >= well_regarded and silver >= 500

unlocks.what_it_gives: A stock of your own at this port (the House tab, Stores): goods left there are not aboard; buy in the cheap season, sell in the dear. A free winter berth and a roof for the crew. A factor needs it. The plot is an instance of works_793.json plot: 12 d a year to the lord of the port at Martinmas, and the house works (storehouse, well, jetty, sheds) are built on it; the price is this port's own. From 889 the plot carries the right to moor along its own width of the hythe (unlock_work_lundenwic_hithe). The danger grows with it: a chronicle raid or burning at this port takes the stock unless it was moved or buried. Rumour comes first.
unlocks.source: Sawyer S 346 (889) and S 1628 (898 or 899), from memory (?); Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 886; price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A house among the Frisians at Eoforwic
unlocks.what_it_is: There was a colony of Frisian merchants at York before 793: about 773 one of them killed a local lord's son in a quarrel, and they all fled for fear of the kin, the young Liudger with them. They came back.

how_won.plain: A Frisian already there stands surety for you before the reeve.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = eoforwic and standing >= known and silver >= 350

unlocks.what_it_gives: A stock of your own at this port (the House tab, Stores): goods left there are not aboard; buy in the cheap season, sell in the dear. A free winter berth and a roof for the crew. A factor needs it. The plot is an instance of works_793.json plot: 12 d a year to the lord of the port at Martinmas, and the house works (storehouse, well, jetty, sheds) are built on it; the price is this port's own. Among your own people: the first to hear what any Frisian ship brought. The danger grows with it: a chronicle raid or burning at this port takes the stock unless it was moved or buried. Rumour comes first.
unlocks.source: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.11-12 (?); the Coppergate tenements laid out c. 900-935; price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A house in the Frisians' quarter at Mogontia
unlocks.what_it_is: The best part of Mainz, 'where the Frisians lived', burned in 886: so the Frisians had a quarter there worth an annalist's notice.

how_won.plain: Bought from a Frisian who is going home, with the archbishop's steward as witness.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and standing >= known and silver >= 400

unlocks.what_it_gives: A stock of your own at this port (the House tab, Stores): goods left there are not aboard; buy in the cheap season, sell in the dear. A free winter berth and a roof for the crew. A factor needs it. The plot is an instance of works_793.json plot: 12 d a year to the lord of the port at Martinmas, and the house works (storehouse, well, jetty, sheds) are built on it; the price is this port's own. Wine bought at the vintage and kept here is sold at Dorestad in the dear months.
unlocks.source: Annales Fuldenses 886 (?); price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: A man at Lundenwic
unlocks.what_it_is: A kinsman or an old hand of the house who stays the year on the Strand, lodges with an English host and answers to the reeve.

how_won.plain: Hold a plot or a host's friendship there, and leave a man the house trusts.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = lundenwic and (flag.unlock_plot_lundenwic or port.best_feeling >= friendly) and silver >= 120

unlocks.what_it_gives: A man of the house at this port (role factor in npc_roles_793.json; a person with a name, a trait, a want and a fear). He keeps the stock, sells what you leave, buys at the right season by standing orders (three slots and one rule: research_scale_to_fleets.md 4.4), and sends word by every ship coming your way: a letter is a card, and as old as the ship that carried it. His keep is 120 d a year, paid at the winter reckoning. His honesty is learned over years, from the tally and the tale. Where the house builds him one, his house is works_793.json factor_house. By the law of Kent a host answers for the guest he has kept three nights: your man's host answers for him, and takes a gift for it.
unlocks.source: Laws of Hlothhere and Eadric c. 15 and 16 (npc_roles_793.json host, reeve); research_scale_to_fleets.md 2 and 4.5

unlocks.name: A man at Eoforwic
unlocks.what_it_is: One of the Frisians of York, who has lived there long enough to have an English wife and an opinion on the king.

how_won.plain: Hold the plot there, or be a fast friend of a Frisian of the colony.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = eoforwic and (flag.unlock_plot_eoforwic or port.best_feeling >= fast_friend) and silver >= 120

unlocks.what_it_gives: A man of the house at this port (role factor in npc_roles_793.json; a person with a name, a trait, a want and a fear). He keeps the stock, sells what you leave, buys at the right season by standing orders (three slots and one rule: research_scale_to_fleets.md 4.4), and sends word by every ship coming your way: a letter is a card, and as old as the ship that carried it. His keep is 120 d a year, paid at the winter reckoning. His honesty is learned over years, from the tally and the tale. Where the house builds him one, his house is works_793.json factor_house. Northumbria changes kings often: his letters are the first word of it.
unlocks.source: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.11-12 (?)

unlocks.name: A Christian household at Birka
unlocks.what_it_is: Frideburg of Birka, rich and old, kept her faith for years with no priest, and on her death bed told her daughter Catla to carry her alms to Dorestad, where there were churches and many poor. Such a household is where a Dorestad house leaves its goods.

how_won.plain: Carry something for a Christian of Birka to Dorestad or back, and be friendly with that household.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = birka and year >= 830 and port.best_feeling >= friendly and silver >= 120

unlocks.what_it_gives: A man of the house at this port (role factor in npc_roles_793.json; a person with a name, a trait, a want and a fear). He keeps the stock, sells what you leave, buys at the right season by standing orders (three slots and one rule: research_scale_to_fleets.md 4.4), and sends word by every ship coming your way: a letter is a card, and as old as the ship that carried it. His keep is 120 d a year, paid at the winter reckoning. His honesty is learned over years, from the tally and the tale. Where the house builds him one, his house is works_793.json factor_house. The lake is shut from Martinmas to April: a letter sent in autumn is answered in June.
unlocks.source: Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 20 (Robinson 1921); npc_roles_793.json widow

unlocks.name: A man at Sliesthorp
unlocks.what_it_is: A Dane, or a Frisian married to one, who knows the king's man and the weight of every trader's silver.

how_won.plain: Hold the plot there and speak the tongue in part.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = sliesthorp and flag.unlock_plot_sliesthorp and tongue.old_norse >= 0.5 and silver >= 120

unlocks.what_it_gives: A man of the house at this port (role factor in npc_roles_793.json; a person with a name, a trait, a want and a fear). He keeps the stock, sells what you leave, buys at the right season by standing orders (three slots and one rule: research_scale_to_fleets.md 4.4), and sends word by every ship coming your way: a letter is a card, and as old as the ship that carried it. His keep is 120 d a year, paid at the winter reckoning. His honesty is learned over years, from the tally and the tale. Where the house builds him one, his house is works_793.json factor_house. He hears the Baltic's prices from the ships that come over the portage from the west.
unlocks.source: chronicle_793.json 808-summer-reric-destroyed, 850-hedeby-church

unlocks.name: A man in the Frisians' quarter at Mogontia
unlocks.what_it_is: A Frisian of the Rhine trade who buys at the vintage and knows which abbey's cellarer is short.

how_won.plain: Hold the house there.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and flag.unlock_plot_mogontia and silver >= 120

unlocks.what_it_gives: A man of the house at this port (role factor in npc_roles_793.json; a person with a name, a trait, a want and a fear). He keeps the stock, sells what you leave, buys at the right season by standing orders (three slots and one rule: research_scale_to_fleets.md 4.4), and sends word by every ship coming your way: a letter is a card, and as old as the ship that carried it. His keep is 120 d a year, paid at the winter reckoning. His honesty is learned over years, from the tally and the tale. Where the house builds him one, his house is works_793.json factor_house. He buys wine in October at the vintage price for the spring run.
unlocks.source: Annales Fuldenses 886 (?)

unlocks.name: A host at Quentovic
unlocks.what_it_is: Quentovic was the crossing place for English pilgrims and their letters. A host there lodges them, changes their pennies and hears everything.

how_won.plain: Be a friend of a host there and carry letters for him.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and port.best_feeling >= friendly and silver >= 120

unlocks.what_it_gives: A man of the house at this port (role factor in npc_roles_793.json; a person with a name, a trait, a want and a fear). He keeps the stock, sells what you leave, buys at the right season by standing orders (three slots and one rule: research_scale_to_fleets.md 4.4), and sends word by every ship coming your way: a letter is a card, and as old as the ship that carried it. His keep is 120 d a year, paid at the winter reckoning. His honesty is learned over years, from the tally and the tale. Where the house builds him one, his house is works_793.json factor_house. He is not your man but your host: he takes a twentieth of what he sells for you instead of a keep.
unlocks.source: npc_roles_793.json host, pilgrim; Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12

unlocks.name: A partner in the Norse way
unlocks.what_it_is: Félag: 'to lay property together'. Two men put goods or a ship in one stock and share what comes back. The word is cut on many rune stones: Thorulf raised a stone at Hedeby for Erik 'his partner', a ship's master; at Aarhus four men raised one for a partner who 'owned a ship with Arni'.

how_won.plain: Eat at a Dane's or a Northman's table, speak his tongue, trade beside him two summers, and swear it before witnesses.
how_won.when: moored and tongue.old_norse >= 0.5 and port.best_feeling >= fast_friend

unlocks.what_it_gives: A sworn partner who sails a second boat for the house (research_scale_to_fleets.md, stage 3). Only a route you have sailed three times yourself, end to end, can be given to him, with orders in words. You see his boat only where your own eyes or a letter can. He takes his share of what his boat makes. Half and half. He brings his own boat (unlock_ship_norse_small_boat or better) and the Norse ports' good will: his word is your surety where you are a stranger. If he dies, you raise his stone.
unlocks.source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Félag, read 4 Oct 2026; runes_793.json hedeby_dr1; the Aarhus stone DR 68, wording from memory (?)

unlocks.name: A brother, a sister's son or a wife's brother
unlocks.what_it_is: A boat was often owned in shares among kin, and the second boat was sailed by a son, a brother or an in-law. Kin are loyal. They are not always good skippers.

how_won.plain: A grown kinsman of the house, by birth or by marriage (any unlock_kin_ flag), who has sailed two seasons in your boat.

unlocks.what_it_gives: A sworn partner who sails a second boat for the house (research_scale_to_fleets.md, stage 3). Only a route you have sailed three times yourself, end to end, can be given to him, with orders in words. You see his boat only where your own eyes or a letter can. He takes his share of what his boat makes. He takes a third and does not leave for a better offer. His skill is whatever it is: the tally shows it.
unlocks.source: research_scale_to_fleets.md section 2 (shares and kin)

unlocks.name: A neighbour, in shares
unlocks.what_it_is: The neighbour on the next plot has seasoned timber and no silver. You pay the wright, he sails her, and the boat is owned half and half.

how_won.plain: Offered some winter to a house with silver to spare (the winter card harbour.winter.shares).

unlocks.what_it_gives: A sworn partner who sails a second boat for the house (research_scale_to_fleets.md, stage 3). Only a route you have sailed three times yourself, end to end, can be given to him, with orders in words. You see his boat only where your own eyes or a letter can. He takes his share of what his boat makes. Half and half. He is a good skipper and knows it: after three good years he asks for more, or for a boat of his own. (A quarter of another man's ship, with no say in where she sails, is works_793.json ship_share.)
unlocks.source: research_scale_to_fleets.md sections 2 and 3; winter_793.json harbour.winter.shares

unlocks.name: A widow's stake
unlocks.what_it_is: A widow holds her dead husband's house, his storehouse or his share in a ship, and needs someone to sail it. Sigrid of Mervalla raised a stone for her husband Svein, who 'often sailed a dear ship to Semgallen, round Domesnes'.

how_won.plain: Bring a lost man's goods or his last word home to his widow, honestly.

unlocks.what_it_gives: A sworn partner who sails a second boat for the house (research_scale_to_fleets.md, stage 3). Only a route you have sailed three times yourself, end to end, can be given to him, with orders in words. You see his boat only where your own eyes or a letter can. He takes his share of what his boat makes. She puts in silver or a hull and takes half; you find the skipper. She does not sail, so the route is yours to choose. Cheat her once and every port of her people hears it.
unlocks.source: runes_793.json mervalla_so198; npc_roles_793.json widow; Rimbert, Vita Anskarii 20

unlocks.name: The Vlie
unlocks.what_it_is: The Fli: the outflow of the Almere, the inland lake of the Frisians, to the open sea. The law of the Frisians counts their middle land 'between the Fli and the Sincfal'. It is the Frisian road north to Ripa and Sliesthorp, and its channel between the sands moves after every winter.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore. A skipper of Medemelacha knows it best.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = medemelacha or port.id = wijnaldum or port.id = dorestad)

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: Lex Frisionum (c. 802): 'inter Fli et Sincfalam'; npc_roles_793.json pilot

unlocks.name: The mouth of the Maas
unlocks.what_it_is: Where the Maas and the southern Rhine arms meet the sea among shifting banks. The market of Witla lay there until the Northmen burned it in 836.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore. The fishermen of the mouth sell the knowledge for a knife.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = witla or port.id = walichrum or port.id = dorestad)

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: Annales Bertiniani 836 (chronicle_793.json 836-witla-antwerp-burned); npc_text_encounters.md sample lines on the Maas mouth

unlocks.name: The Wantsum
unlocks.what_it_is: The channel that parts Thanet from Kent: about three furlongs broad in Bede's day and fordable in only two places. Sarre lies in the middle of it. It is the sheltered way from the Channel into the Thames, inside the North Foreland.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore. The ferrymen of Sarre know its two fords.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = sarre or port.id = fordwic or port.id = dofras)

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: Bede, Historia ecclesiastica I.25 (the river Wantsum, three furlongs over, passable in two places)

unlocks.name: The Thames sands and the tide to Lundenwic
unlocks.what_it_is: A wide mouth full of sands, then sixty kilometres of river where the tide does the work: a ship that takes the flood at the right hour is carried to the Strand, and one that misses it waits six hours at anchor.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = lundenwic or port.id = sarre)

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: tide and distance: the game's tide model; the law of Hlothhere and Eadric c. 16 for Lundenwic as the Kentish men's market

unlocks.name: The Humber and the Ouse
unlocks.what_it_is: A broad brown estuary with banks that walk, then the Ouse, tidal all the way up to Eoforwic. Alcuin called York a market of land and sea, where ships come from far over the ocean.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore. A Frisian of the York colony teaches it to his own people.

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: Alcuin, Versus de patribus, regibus et sanctis Euboricensis ecclesiae (York as emporium) (?)

unlocks.name: The bar of the Canche
unlocks.what_it_is: Quentovic lies some way up the Canche behind dunes and a bar that dries. Ships wait outside for the flood, in full view of the toll.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore.

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: site of Quentovic at La Calotterie on the Canche (excavations of D. Hill, 1980s) (?)

unlocks.name: The loops of the Seine
unlocks.what_it_is: From the sea to Rotomagus the river turns back on itself again and again, and a wave runs up it with the spring tides. Above Rotomagus the towpath begins.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = rotomagus or port.id = parisius)

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: the tidal bore of the lower Seine (the mascaret); its first written notice is later than 1066 (?)

unlocks.name: The Slie
unlocks.what_it_is: A narrow arm of the Baltic that runs forty kilometres into Jutland, with shoals at its mouth and a bend every mile. At its head lies Sliesthorp; from there it is a short haul overland to the rivers of the western sea.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore. The ferryman on the Slie knows it.

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: Annales regni Francorum 804 and 808 (portus Sliesthorp); riddles_793.json, a ferryman on the Schlei

unlocks.name: The Limfjord
unlocks.what_it_is: The water road through the north of Jutland from the western sea to the Kattegat. It saves a ship the Skaw, the worst headland of the Danes. Its western mouth was open in this age and closed with sand afterwards.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = ripa or port.id = hleidr or port.id = sliesthorp)

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: the western opening of the Limfjord closed about 1100-1200 (?); Adam of Bremen on the passage round the Skaw (texts_793.json adam)

unlocks.name: The way into the lake of the Svear
unlocks.what_it_is: Birka lies on an island in a lake that is still an arm of the sea. The way in is by narrow sounds among skerries, the southern one growing shallower every lifetime as the land rises.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = birka or port.id = helgo or port.id = uppsalir)

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: land uplift and the southern entrance at Södertälje, too shallow by about 1000 (?); chronicle_793.json 975-birka-sigtuna

unlocks.name: Ladoga and the Volkhov
unlocks.what_it_is: Across a lake as wide as a sea, then up a river to Aldeigjuborg, and above it the rapids where goods are carried round on the bank. Beyond lies the river road to the Greeks and the dirhams.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore. A Rus trader who winters on the Volkhov teaches it.

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: riddles_793.json, a Rus trader on the Volkhov; the Volkhov rapids above Staraya Ladoga (?)

unlocks.name: The Estmere and the Ilfing
unlocks.what_it_is: Wulfstan's road: the Vistula's mouth, the wide shallow Estmere behind its sand spit, and the river Ilfing that runs out of the lake on whose shore Truso stands.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore. With Wulfstan's account in the chest (text.wulfstan) one hired passage is enough.

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: texts_793.json wulfstan (Bosworth 1859)

unlocks.name: The Loire mouth and the bay of the salt
unlocks.what_it_is: Sandbanks, a strong ebb, and the island of Herio with its monks and salt pans lying off to the south. The salt ships of all the west come here in summer.

how_won.plain: Hire the local pilot on three calls and come through without touching; or sail it three times end to end yourself; or be taught it over a winter by a factor or partner of that shore.
how_won.when: moored and (port.id = namnetis or port.id = herio)

unlocks.what_it_gives: On this water: no pilot's fee (act:hire_pilot is not needed), the grounding check on the bar is passed as 'sure', the day stick shows the tide window before the course is set, and a route through it can be given to a skipper.
unlocks.source: npc_roles_793.json salter (the monks' pans at Herio); chronicle_793.json for the raids on Noirmoutier

unlocks.name: A sounding line and lead
unlocks.what_it_is: A lead weight on a marked line, its hollow foot filled with tallow to bring up a pinch of the bottom: sand, shell or mud tells a seaman where he is. The English had words for the sounding rod and the sounding line.

how_won.plain: Bought from a smith with two units of lead, or taken from a wreck.

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship. In fog or at night within a day of a coast, grounding checks are one step better (doubtful to likely, likely to sure), and the fuzzy area of her position on the chart is halved near a bar she has sounded before.
unlocks.source: Old English glosses sundgyrd and sundline (?); soundings in Acts 27.28; goods_793.json lead

unlocks.name: An iron anchor
unlocks.what_it_is: Most small boats lay to a stone lashed in a wooden frame. An anchor of iron with a length of chain holds where a stone drags: the Oseberg ship of 834 had one, and the Ladby ship of about 925 had one with eleven metres of chain.

how_won.plain: Forged to order by a smith: four units of bar iron and his work.

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship. At anchor in a gale the drag check is one step better. She can lie off a beach she cannot be hauled up on.
unlocks.source: the Oseberg anchor (834) and the Ladby anchor and chain (c. 925): museum finds; goods_793.json bar_iron; price a guess (?)

unlocks.name: Rigging of walrus hide
unlocks.what_it_is: Ohthere told King Alfred that the Finnas paid him tribute in 'ship-ropes' of whale hide and seal hide, sixty ells long. Cut in one spiral strip from a walrus skin, it is the strongest rope in the north.

how_won.plain: Two units of walrus_rope aboard, fitted at any yard.

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship. Rigging does not part in a gale (the mast-gone result is one step less likely), and the anchor cable holds.
unlocks.source: texts_793.json ohthere (Bosworth 1859); goods_793.json walrus_rope

unlocks.name: A tilt for the nights
unlocks.what_it_is: A tent of cloth stretched over the boat on a frame of carved boards when she lies at anchor or on a beach. The Oseberg and Gokstad ships were buried with theirs.

how_won.plain: Two units of sailcloth and a day's work.

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship. The crew's health does not fall for cold or rain on nights spent aboard or on a beach, and no lodging is paid where there is a beach.
unlocks.source: the tent frames of the Oseberg (834) and Gokstad (c. 900) ships; goods_793.json sailcloth

unlocks.name: A new sail, fulled and greased
unlocks.what_it_is: A sail is the dearest thing aboard after the hull: the wool of many sheep and a winter of women's work, woven tight, fulled and rubbed with fat and ochre so it holds the wind.

how_won.plain: Six units of sailcloth, or a winter's weaving in the house (the winter card harbour.winter.weaving).

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship. Speed under sail up by one part in twenty; she points a little closer to the wind (closest_to_wind_deg minus 2). It wears: after eight years it is an old sail again.
unlocks.source: Viking Ship Museum, Roskilde, on woollen sails and their cost (?); goods_793.json sailcloth

unlocks.name: A tacking spar
unlocks.what_it_is: A pole that pushes the weather edge of the square sail forward so the ship can work closer to the wind. The Norse word for it, beitiáss, is written down only later; the replicas of the Skuldelev ships cannot do without it.

how_won.plain: Shown by a Norse steersman; cut from an ash pole.

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship. She sails closer to the wind (closest_to_wind_deg minus 6) when a man is spared to tend it.
unlocks.source: the word is attested after 1066; the date it came into use is not known (?). Viking Ship Museum sailing trials

unlocks.name: A strake added
unlocks.what_it_is: The wright scarfs a new plank along each side above the old top strake. She sits the same and carries more, and takes less water over the side.

how_won.plain: A winter's work for a wright (the winter card harbour.winter.rebuild).

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship of 12 m or less. Cargo up by a fifth, freeboard up by a plank's width (gale_fragility one tenth better). She rows heavier.
unlocks.source: ordinary clinker practice; winter_793.json harbour.winter.rebuild

unlocks.name: A boat towed astern
unlocks.what_it_is: A big ship carries or tows a small one for landing on a beach, for laying out an anchor and for the day she sinks.

how_won.plain: Only for a ship of 12 m or more. Buy a small boat (unlock_ship_norse_small_boat or a west_small_boat).

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship. She can trade at a beach landing she cannot reach herself. In a wreck the men are 'likely' saved, not 'doubtful'.
unlocks.source: the three small boats of the Gokstad burial (c. 900)

unlocks.name: Decks fore and aft
unlocks.what_it_is: The late cargo ships are decked at bow and stern with an open hold between: the goods stay drier and the men have somewhere to stand.

how_won.plain: Only when a ship of 12 m or more is built or rebuilt, from about 990.

unlocks.what_it_gives: Fitted to one ship. Spoilage of cargo by spray and rain halved.
unlocks.source: the Klåstad ship (990s) and Skuldelev 1 and 3 (c. 1030-1040): ship_classes_793.json later_types_not_in_table

unlocks.name: A longer causeway at Dorestad
unlocks.what_it_is: The river left Dorestad a little every year, and every plot-holder built his timber causeway further out after it: rows of posts, brushwood and planks, in the end hundreds of feet long.

how_won.plain: Paid for by a plot-holder, or given finished by a chain.
how_won.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.unlock_plot_dorestad

unlocks.what_it_gives: At Dorestad it must be done again about every twelve years as the river moves, or the plot is cut off from the stream and the work is lost.
